mod0_quiz.prompt: By the time the seminar starts next Monday, Dr. Alvarez ______ her final report for over three weeks.

options.A: writes
options.B: has been writing

mod0_quiz.why_right: Futuro perfeito contínuo: ação iniciada no passado, contínua até um ponto futuro específico ("by the time... next Monday"), com ênfase na duração ("for over three weeks").
mod0_quiz.why_wrong: (A) presente simples ignora a duração; (B) presente perfeito contínuo não projeta para o futuro; (D) passado contínuo não conecta com o marco temporal futuro.

mod0_quiz.prompt: The new policy was designed to reduce administrative costs; ______, early data suggests it has increased them.

options.A: furthermore
options.B: as a result

mod0_quiz.why_right: O conector precisa sinalizar contraste + ironia entre a intenção da política (reduzir custos) e o resultado real (aumentou custos) — "paradoxically" captura essa contradição inesperada.
mod0_quiz.why_wrong: (A) e (B) são de continuidade/consequência lógica, incompatíveis com contraste; (D) sinaliza semelhança, o oposto do que a frase exige.

mod0_quiz.prompt: The committee's decision to postpone the vote was widely seen as an attempt to ______ growing public criticism.

options.A: defer
options.B: exacerbate

mod0_quiz.why_right: "Circumvent" (contornar/evitar) encaixa com a lógica de adiar o voto para não enfrentar diretamente a crítica pública.
mod0_quiz.why_wrong: (A) "defer" é próximo mas não captura a ideia de "evitar/desviar" a crítica em si — refere-se a adiar algo, não contornar algo; (B) significa piorar, sentido oposto; (D) significa endossar, sentido oposto.

mod0_quiz.prompt: If the funding request ______ approved last quarter, the lab would already have hired two new researchers.

options.A: was
options.B: were

mod0_quiz.why_right: Condicional tipo 3 (passado hipotético): a oração principal usa "would have hired" implícito na lógica ("would already have hired"), exigindo past perfect na condicional ("had been approved").
mod0_quiz.why_wrong: (A) e (B) são formas de passado simples/subjuntivo incompatíveis com a estrutura de tipo 3; (D) é present perfect, tempo errado para hipótese no passado.

mod0_quiz.prompt:
Choose the option that best completes the sentence with correct word order and meaning:
Despite ______, the research team published their findings ahead of schedule.

options.A: numerous setbacks facing
options.B: facing numerous setbacks

mod0_quiz.why_right: Ordem correta: verbo no gerúndio + objeto ("facing numerous setbacks") após "despite", seguindo a estrutura padrão preposição + gerúndio + complemento.
mod0_quiz.why_wrong: (A) inverte adjetivo e verbo de forma não natural; (C) e (D) quebram a ordem sintática do inglês (adjetivo deve preceder o substantivo, verbo deve preceder o objeto).

mod0_quiz.prompt: Coral reefs are highly sensitive to temperature change; ______, even a one-degree rise can trigger mass bleaching events.

options.A: nevertheless
options.B: in contrast

mod0_quiz.why_right: A segunda oração é uma consequência lógica direta da sensibilidade térmica mencionada na primeira — "accordingly" (consequentemente) é o conector de causa-efeito correto.
mod0_quiz.why_wrong: (A) e (B) sinalizam contraste, incompatível com a relação de causa-efeito; (D) sinaliza simultaneidade, não consequência.

mod0_quiz.prompt: The professor asked students to ______ their arguments with at least two peer-reviewed sources.

options.A: substantiate
options.B: fabricate

mod0_quiz.why_right: "Substantiate an argument" é a collocation acadêmica padrão para "sustentar/comprovar um argumento com evidências".
mod0_quiz.why_wrong: (B) significa fabricar/inventar, sentido oposto ao contexto acadêmico legítimo; (C) significa aliviar, sem relação; (D) significa diminuir, sentido oposto.

mod0_quiz.topic: Gramática (relative clauses / estrutura complexa — relevante para Listen and Repeat)
mod0_quiz.prompt: The proposal, ______ implications had not been fully considered, was rejected by the board.

options.A: that its
options.B: which its

mod0_quiz.why_right: "Whose" é o pronome relativo possessivo correto para conectar "the proposal" a "its implications" sem repetir "its".
mod0_quiz.why_wrong: (A) "that its" é gramaticalmente incorreto (that não aceita possessivo desta forma); (B) "which its" repete a posse de forma redundante e incorreta; (D) "who's" é contração de "who is", não um possessivo.

mod0_quiz.topic: Registro e função comunicativa (relevante para Write an Email)
mod0_quiz.prompt: Choose the sentence with the register most appropriate for a formal email to a university admissions office requesting a deadline extension:

options.A: Hey, just wondering if I could get a bit more time to send my stuff over?
options.B: I am writing to respectfully request a short extension to the submission deadline due to a documented medical circumstance.
options.C: Give me more time please, it's urgent and I really need it.
options.D: So I was thinking maybe you guys could push the date back for me?

mod0_quiz.why_right: Registro formal, verbos modais de cortesia ("I am writing to respectfully request"), justificativa objetiva — adequado para comunicação institucional, exatamente o padrão exigido em Write an Email.
mod0_quiz.why_wrong: (A), (C) e (D) usam registro coloquial, contrações e informalidade excessiva ("just wondering", "you guys", "please" isolado) — inadequados para o contexto navegacional acadêmico formal.

mod0_quiz.topic: Compreensão inferencial (relevante para Read an Academic Passage / Listen to an Academic Talk)
mod0_quiz.prompt:
"Although the pilot program showed promising results in urban districts, researchers cautioned against broad conclusions, noting that participation rates in rural areas remained too low to generalize."

What can be inferred from this statement?

options.A: The pilot program failed in urban districts.
options.B: Rural areas were excluded from the pilot program entirely.
options.C: The results may not represent the population as a whole.

mod0_quiz.why_right: O texto explicitamente qualifica os resultados como não-generalizáveis devido à baixa participação rural — a inferência lógica direta é que os resultados podem não representar a população total.
mod0_quiz.why_wrong: (A) contradiz o texto (resultados foram "promissores", não um fracasso); (B) exagera — "baixa participação" não é "exclusão total"; (D) é uma conclusão não sustentada pelo texto, que apenas pede cautela, não cancelamento.

mod1_drills.title: Drill 1 — Complete the Words: reconstrução de texto
mod1_drills.objective: Para cada lacuna numerada, escolha a opção que reconstrói o texto de forma gramatical, lexicalmente natural e coerente com o sentido geral. Tempo alvo: 6 minutos para os 8 itens.
mod1_drills.passage_html:
TEXT: A Message From the Office Manager

Hi team,

I wanted to send a quick note before the long weekend. As most of you already (1)_____, the building's heating system will be shut down for scheduled maintenance from Friday evening through Monday morning. Please make sure you (2)_____ any equipment that shouldn't be left running unattended, and take home anything that might be sensitive to temperature changes over the weekend.

The maintenance crew has assured us that the work will be (3)_____ before Monday, so there shouldn't be any disruption when everyone (4)_____ back to the office. However, if the weather turns unexpectedly cold, the building may take a little longer than usual to (5)_____ up again — so please dress in layers just in case.

If you have any questions or concerns, don't (6)_____ to reach out to facilities directly. We'd rather you ask a question that turns out to be unnecessary than (7)_____ a real problem over the weekend.

Thanks for your patience, and enjoy the (8)_____ time off!

items.prompt: Lacuna (1)

options.A: know
options.B: knows

items.explanation: "As most of you already know" pede presente simples na 3ª pessoa do plural (forma base, sem -s) — construção fixa comum em avisos. (B) quebra a concordância; (C) exigiria auxiliar ("have known"); (D) não completa o tempo verbal da oração.

items.prompt: Lacuna (2)

options.A: turn off
options.B: turn down

items.explanation: "Turn off equipment" = desligar equipamento, a collocation exata para o contexto de manutenção/segurança. (B) = diminuir intensidade; (C) = descobrir-se/comparecer; (D) = virar/entregar — nenhum se encaixa aqui.

items.prompt: Lacuna (3)

options.A: complete
options.B: completing

items.explanation: "Will be _____" pede particípio passado para a voz passiva. "Will be completed" é a estrutura passiva padrão. As outras formas quebram a estrutura "be + particípio".

items.prompt: Lacuna (4)

options.A: come
options.B: comes

items.explanation: "Everyone" é gramaticalmente singular, então o verbo vai para a 3ª pessoa do singular: "comes back". (A) quebra a concordância; (C) exigiria auxiliar; (D) é agramatical ("will" nunca é seguido de verbo com -s).

items.prompt: Lacuna (5)

options.A: warm
options.B: warms

items.explanation: "To _____ up again" pede o infinitivo (verbo base) após "to". "Warm up" é o phrasal verb certo para um ambiente recuperando temperatura — as outras opções quebram essa estrutura.

items.prompt: Lacuna (6)

options.A: hesitate
options.B: hesitating

items.explanation: "Don't _____ to reach out" pede verbo base após o imperativo negativo "don't". "Don't hesitate to + verbo" é expressão fixa clássica em comunicação profissional.

items.prompt: Lacuna (7)

options.A: miss
options.B: lose

items.explanation: Estrutura paralela "ask a question... than _____ a real problem" pede verbo base após "than". "Lose" mantém o contraste lógico: preferir perguntar a deixar o problema se agravar. "Miss"/"waste"/"fail" não combinam com "problem" da mesma forma direta.

items.prompt: Lacuna (8)

options.A: extend
options.B: extending

items.explanation: "The _____ time off" pede um adjetivo (particípio usado como adjetivo) antes do substantivo. "Extended time off" = folga prolongada. As outras formas não funcionam como modificador de substantivo nessa posição.

mod1_drills.title: Drill 2 — Read in Daily Life: texto curto não-acadêmico
mod1_drills.objective: Leia o texto uma vez, identificando formato, remetente, destinatário e propósito. Responda às 4 questões. Tempo alvo: 3 minutos.
mod1_drills.passage_html:
TEXT: A social media post from a local bakery

🥐 Riverside Bakery — Posted 2 hours ago

Big news, everyone! Starting next Tuesday, we're extending our weekday hours — open at 6:30 AM instead of 7:00 AM, so early risers can grab their coffee and croissants before work. 🌅

Quick heads-up though: because of the earlier opening, our weekday sourdough batch will now go into the oven the night before instead of first thing in the morning. It'll still be baked fresh daily, just on a slightly different schedule — so if you're used to catching it warm right out of the oven at 8 AM, it might be ready a little earlier now. Come say hi and let us know what you think of the new hours!

Weekend hours are unchanged (8 AM–3 PM, same as always).

items.prompt: What is the main purpose of this post?

options.A: To announce that the bakery is closing early on weekdays
options.B: To inform customers about a change to weekday opening hours
options.C: To apologize for a delay in the sourdough baking schedule
options.D: To advertise a new type of bread being introduced

items.explanation: O post inteiro gira em torno de um único anúncio: abrir mais cedo nos dias de semana. (A) inverte o sentido (é abertura mais cedo, não fechamento); (C) o texto não pede desculpas; (D) nenhum pão novo é introduzido, só o horário de forno muda.

items.prompt: According to the post, what will change about the sourdough bread?

options.A: It will no longer be baked fresh every day.
options.B: It will only be available on weekends.
options.C: It will be baked the night before instead of the same morning.
options.D: It will be replaced with a different type of bread.

items.explanation: O texto afirma exatamente isso. (A) o texto diz "it'll still be baked fresh daily"; (B) nada indica restrição a fins de semana; (D) não há substituição de produto.

items.prompt: What can be inferred about the bakery's weekend hours?

options.A: They will also move to 6:30 AM starting next Tuesday.
options.B: They remain the same as they were before this announcement.
options.C: They have not yet been decided.
options.D: They will be shortened to match the new weekday schedule.

items.explanation: A última linha afirma diretamente: "Weekend hours are unchanged". (A) e (D) contradizem o texto; (C) o texto não deixa isso em aberto.

items.prompt: The overall tone of this post is best described as:

options.A: formal and apologetic
options.B: friendly and informative

items.explanation: Emojis, saudação casual, convite pessoal e tom positivo caracterizam um registro amigável e informativo. Não há tom apologético, urgência/alerta, ou impessoalidade.

mod1_drills.title: Drill 3 — Read an Academic Passage
mod1_drills.objective: Leia a passagem completa uma vez (ela é curta o suficiente para isso). Responda às 6 questões. Tempo alvo: 6 minutos.
mod1_drills.passage_html:
PASSAGE: Bioluminescence in Marine Organisms

Bioluminescence — the production and emission of light by a living organism — is remarkably common in the ocean, appearing in bacteria, jellyfish, fish, and even some sharks. Unlike the light produced by a bulb, which wastes most of its energy as heat, bioluminescent light is generated through a highly efficient chemical reaction, typically involving a light-emitting molecule called luciferin and an enzyme called luciferase. Because so little energy is lost as heat, biologists sometimes refer to this phenomenon as "cold light."

The functions of bioluminescence vary considerably across species, though three purposes appear again and again. Some organisms use light defensively: certain species of squid release a luminous cloud instead of ink, startling predators and buying time to escape. Others use it as a hunting tool. The anglerfish, perhaps the most famous example, dangles a glowing lure above its mouth to attract smaller prey close enough to seize. Still others use light for communication, particularly in the deep sea, where darkness is nearly absolute and visual signals cannot rely on ambient light. Certain species of ostracods, tiny crustaceans, produce synchronized light displays to attract mates — a strategy so distinctive that in some regions it has been used by local fishers as a marker of species presence.

What makes bioluminescence especially interesting to evolutionary biologists is that it did not evolve just once. Genetic and biochemical evidence indicates that the capacity for bioluminescence has arisen independently dozens of times across unrelated lineages, using different chemical pathways to achieve a similar outcome. This pattern, in which unrelated organisms evolve similar traits independently, is known as convergent evolution, and bioluminescence is considered one of its most striking examples precisely because the same functional result — producing light efficiently — has been "reinvented" so many times by evolution.

items.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?

options.A: Bioluminescence is a rare adaptation found only in a few deep-sea species.
options.B: Bioluminescence is a widespread, chemically efficient trait that serves multiple functions and evolved independently many times.
options.C: The anglerfish is the most important example of bioluminescence among marine organisms.
options.D: Bioluminescent light is less efficient than artificial light produced by a bulb.

items.explanation: A passagem cobre três eixos: o que é o fenômeno e sua eficiência química, suas múltiplas funções, e sua origem evolutiva independente. Só (B) sintetiza os três. (A) contradiz o texto ("remarkably common"); (C) é um detalhe; (D) inverte o sentido do texto.

items.prompt: According to the passage, why is bioluminescent light sometimes called "cold light"?

options.A: It only occurs in cold, deep-sea environments.
options.B: It is produced by organisms that live in low-temperature waters.
options.C: The chemical reaction that produces it wastes very little energy as heat.
options.D: It appears blue or white in color, resembling ice.

items.explanation: O texto afirma isso diretamente com relação causal explícita ("because so little energy is lost as heat"). As outras opções confundem o termo com temperatura ambiente ou cor, o que o texto não sustenta.

items.prompt: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in the passage as a function of bioluminescence?

options.A: Startling predators
options.B: Attracting prey

items.explanation: O parágrafo 2 lista três funções: defesa, caça e comunicação/atração de parceiros. Regulação de temperatura corporal nunca é mencionada — as outras três estão todas explicitamente no texto.

items.prompt: It can be inferred from paragraph 2 that in deep-sea environments:

options.A: visual communication is impossible for any species
options.B: organisms rely on producing their own light because there is little to no ambient light
options.C: most species have evolved to lose their sense of sight entirely
options.D: bioluminescence is used exclusively for hunting, not communication

items.explanation: O texto liga diretamente a comunicação por luz própria à ausência de luz ambiente no fundo do mar. (A) é extremo demais; (C) não é sustentado pelo texto; (D) contradiz o próprio parágrafo, que lista comunicação como função distinta.

items.prompt: Why does the author mention that bioluminescence "did not evolve just once" in paragraph 3?

options.A: To argue that bioluminescence is less biologically significant than previously thought
options.B: To introduce and support the claim that bioluminescence is a notable example of convergent evolution
options.C: To explain why some marine species have gone extinct
options.D: To compare bioluminescence with the evolution of eyesight in mammals

items.explanation: A frase é seguida imediatamente por uma menção a evolução convergente — a menção de evolução independente serve para embasar esse conceito, foco do parágrafo. Nenhuma das outras opções tem base no texto.

items.prompt: The word "striking" in paragraph 3 is closest in meaning to:

options.A: violent
options.B: notable

items.explanation: "Striking" no contexto de "one of its most striking examples" significa notável/impressionante. "Violent" pertence a outro campo semântico; "accidental" e "doubtful" invertem o tom confiante do texto.

mod2_drills.title: Drill 1 — Listen and Choose a Response (Escala 0 — Sem Anotação)
mod2_drills.objective: Leia cada fala UMA vez, sem reler. Escolha a resposta que soa mais natural e pragmaticamente correta. Tempo alvo: 12 segundos por item. Simula o ritmo do router — cada item é um estímulo independente, sem passagem compartilhada.

items.prompt: Speaker: "I was going to grab lunch before the seminar, but I don't think there's enough time now."

options.A: "That's fine, I already ate breakfast."
options.B: "Yeah, we should probably just head straight there."
options.D: "I had lunch there last week too."

items.explanation: O falante sinaliza falta de tempo para almoçar; a resposta natural reconhece isso e propõe a ação consequente (ir direto). As outras opções ignoram a urgência mencionada.

items.prompt: Speaker: "Do you mind if I borrow your notes from Tuesday's class? I was out sick."

options.A: "Sure, no problem — I'll send them over tonight."
options.B: "I hope you feel better soon, though."

items.explanation: Pedido direto exige resposta direta de concessão. (A) concede e oferece um plano concreto; as outras mudam de assunto ou não respondem ao pedido.

items.prompt: Speaker: "Honestly, I'm not sure this draft is ready to submit."

options.A: "The deadline isn't until Friday, right?"
options.B: "What do you think it still needs?"

items.explanation: O falante expressa insegurança sobre a qualidade do rascunho; a resposta natural busca entender o problema específico. As outras ignoram a preocupação expressa.

items.prompt: Speaker: "You're not still planning to walk to campus in this weather, are you?"

options.A: "No, I'll probably catch the bus instead."
options.B: "The campus is only ten minutes away."
options.D: "It rained a lot last semester too."

items.explanation: É uma pergunta retórica que expressa preocupação com o plano; a resposta natural revisa o plano. As outras reforçam o plano problemático ou são irrelevantes.

items.prompt: Speaker: "I heard the registrar's office changed their hours."

options.A: "I registered for four classes this term."
options.B: "Really? Do you know the new schedule?"
options.C: "The office is on the second floor."

items.explanation: Informação nova é compartilhada; a resposta natural demonstra interesse e busca detalhe. (A) e (D) confundem "registrar-se" com "registrar" no sentido de horário; (C) não responde à informação dada.

mod2_drills.title: Drill 2 — Listen to a Conversation (Escala 1 — Nota Mínima)
mod2_drills.objective: Leia a transcrição UMA vez, anotando apenas o essencial (3–5 palavras por turno relevante). Depois responda às 4 questões usando só suas notas mínimas. Tempo alvo: 3 minutos total.
mod2_drills.passage_html:
TRANSCRIPT — AT THE STUDENT ADVISING OFFICE

Narrator: Listen to a conversation between a student and an academic advisor.

Student: Hi, I wanted to ask about switching one of my electives. I'm currently in Intro to Statistics, but I think I'd rather take the Data Visualization course instead.

Advisor: Sure, let me check... okay, Data Visualization does have space. But just so you know, it has Statistics as a prerequisite — have you completed that already?

Student: No, that's actually why I wanted to switch — I was hoping to take Data Visualization first and Statistics later.

Advisor: Ah, I see. Unfortunately, that's not possible — the prerequisite is enforced by the system. You'd need to complete Statistics first, or get a written waiver from the Data Visualization instructor.

Student: Okay, that makes sense. Is it worth asking the instructor directly, or is that rarely approved?

Advisor: It's approved sometimes, especially if you have relevant experience — like a coding background. Do you have any?

Student: I do, actually — I took two programming courses last year.

Advisor: Then it's worth emailing her. I'll send you her contact information right now.

items.prompt: Gist-Purpose — Why does the student visit the advising office?

options.A: To complain about a scheduling conflict between two required courses
options.B: To request a change from one elective course to another
options.C: To ask for help registering for classes for the first time
options.D: To find out why she was removed from a course roster

items.explanation: A estudante afirma diretamente que quer trocar de eletiva. Não há conflito de horário mencionado, ela já está matriculada, e (D) nunca é mencionado.

items.prompt: Detail — What problem does the advisor identify?

options.A: The Data Visualization course is already full for the semester
options.B: The student has already failed the Statistics prerequisite once
options.C: Data Visualization requires Statistics as a prerequisite, which the student hasn't completed
options.D: The student is not eligible to take electives outside her major

items.explanation: A conselheira explica claramente o pré-requisito não cumprido. (A) é o oposto (há vaga); (B) e (D) nunca são mencionados.

items.prompt: Understanding the Function — Why does the advisor ask whether the student has a coding background?

options.A: To determine whether the student qualifies for a separate scholarship
options.B: To suggest that the student consider switching majors entirely
options.C: To assess whether the instructor might realistically grant a prerequisite waiver
options.D: To recommend an entirely different course better suited to her skills

items.explanation: A pergunta serve para avaliar se a estudante tem chance real de conseguir uma dispensa do pré-requisito. As outras opções não têm base no texto.

items.prompt: Detail — What does the advisor do at the end of the conversation?

options.A: She enrolls the student in Data Visualization immediately
options.B: She provides the student with the instructor's contact information
options.C: She schedules a follow-up meeting for the following week
options.D: She tells the student to wait until the next semester to decide

items.explanation: A conselheira diz que vai enviar o contato da professora — direto e literal. A matrícula não acontece nesta conversa, e (C)/(D) não são mencionados.

mod2_drills.title: Drill 3 — Listen to an Announcement (Escala 1 — Checklist Auditiva)
mod2_drills.objective: Leia UMA vez. Anote apenas os pontos de checklist (data / local / ação / exceção). Tempo alvo: 2 minutos total.
mod2_drills.passage_html:
TRANSCRIPT — CAMPUS ANNOUNCEMENT

Narrator: Listen to an announcement about a change to library services.

Speaker: Attention, students. Starting next Monday, the Main Library's reading room on the third floor will be closed for renovation through the end of the month. During this period, students will be able to use the East Wing reading room instead, which will remain open on its regular schedule. Please note that reserved study rooms originally booked for the third floor have already been automatically transferred to the East Wing — you do not need to rebook them. However, if your reservation was for a room with audiovisual equipment, please double-check availability, since not all East Wing rooms are equipped. Questions can be directed to the circulation desk.

items.prompt: Detail — When does the reading room closure begin?

options.A: Immediately, starting today
options.B: Next Monday
options.C: At the end of the month

items.explanation: "Starting next Monday... will be closed" — literal e direto. As outras opções distorcem a data.

items.prompt: Detail — According to the announcement, what happens to previously reserved study rooms?

options.A: They are automatically canceled and must be rebooked
options.B: They are automatically transferred to the East Wing
options.C: They remain in the third floor despite the renovation
options.D: They are only honored if confirmed by email in advance

items.explanation: O texto afirma isso diretamente. (A) é o oposto; (C) contradiz a informação central; (D) adiciona uma condição não mencionada.

items.prompt: Understanding the Function — Why does the speaker mention audiovisual equipment specifically?

options.A: To announce that all audiovisual equipment is being permanently removed
options.B: To recommend that students avoid using audiovisual equipment during renovations
options.C: To warn students that not every transferred room has the same equipment as before
options.D: To advertise a new audiovisual equipment rental service in the East Wing

items.explanation: É um aviso prático para quem reservou salas com equipamento, não uma remoção geral nem uma recomendação de evitar uso.

mod2_drills.title: Drill 4 — Listen to an Academic Talk (Escala 2 — Template Reduzido)
mod2_drills.objective: Leia UMA vez, preenchendo o template reduzido. Depois responda as 5 questões com o texto coberto. Tempo alvo: 4 minutos total.
mod2_drills.passage_html:
TRANSCRIPT — ACADEMIC TALK: THE PARADOX OF CHOICE

Narrator: Listen to part of a talk in a psychology class.

Professor: So we've been discussing decision-making, and today I want to bring up something researchers call the paradox of choice. The basic idea is counterintuitive: you'd think more options would always make us happier, but past a certain point, it actually does the opposite.

Here's a classic example. In one well-known study, researchers set up a tasting table in a grocery store — first with six varieties of jam, then later with twenty-four varieties. You'd expect the bigger display to sell more, right? Actually, the smaller display generated significantly more purchases. The larger display attracted more browsers, but far fewer of them actually bought anything.

Why does this happen? Researchers point to two things: decision fatigue and anticipated regret. With more options, comparing them mentally becomes exhausting — that's decision fatigue. And once you do pick something, you start second-guessing whether one of the twenty-three other jams would've been better — that's anticipated regret. Ironically, having more choices can leave people feeling like they're back to square one, unable to commit to anything at all.

Now, this doesn't mean choice itself is bad — a complete absence of options is its own problem. The point is that there's a sweet spot, and past it, additional options stop helping and start actively working against us.

items.prompt: Gist-Content — What is the main idea of this talk?

options.A: Grocery stores should always minimize the number of products they display
options.B: Beyond a certain point, having more options can reduce satisfaction and hinder decisions
options.C: Consumers always prefer smaller displays regardless of the product involved
options.D: Decision fatigue only affects people making purchases in physical stores

items.explanation: A tese central é anunciada logo no início e reforçada no fechamento ("there's a sweet spot..."). As outras opções são extremas demais ou fora do escopo do texto.

items.prompt: Detail — In the jam study described, what happened with the larger display of 24 varieties?

options.A: It attracted more browsers but resulted in fewer actual purchases
options.B: It resulted in both more browsers and more purchases than the smaller display
options.C: It was removed from the store due to low customer interest
options.D: It produced identical sales results to the smaller display

items.explanation: Literal: "attracted more browsers, but far fewer of them actually bought anything." (B) é o oposto; (C) e (D) não têm base no texto.

items.prompt: Understanding Organization — Why does the professor describe the grocery store study in detail?

options.A: To criticize the methodology used by the original researchers
options.B: To provide concrete evidence supporting the paradox of choice
options.C: To introduce an unrelated topic about consumer marketing
options.D: To explain how grocery stores design their product displays

items.explanation: O estudo é apresentado logo após o conceito abstrato ser introduzido — função clássica de exemplo de apoio.

items.prompt: Making Inferences — What can be inferred about the professor's view on having zero options available?

options.A: It would likely be preferable to having too many options
options.B: It would also be problematic, just as too many options are
options.C: It has never been studied by researchers in this field
options.D: It only applies to situations involving grocery shopping

items.explanation: O professor afirma que "a complete absence of options is its own problem" — implica diretamente que zero opções também é problemático.

items.prompt: Vocabulary in Context — What does the professor mean by the expression "back to square one"?

options.A: Making a confident, well-informed final decision
options.B: Returning to a starting point without having made any real progress
options.C: Choosing the first option that was originally presented
options.D: Comparing two options systematically before deciding

items.explanation: É uma expressão idiomática que significa voltar ao ponto de partida sem progresso real — coerente com o contexto de indecisão.
